age.evidence: Purely computational (in silico) study; no live animals were used — 'These tools enabled the high-throughput screening of ADMET parameters and hazards depending on the organ, without the need for animal testing'.

sex.evidence: No animal subjects; only QSAR-predicted rat/mouse LD50 values are reported.

psychedelic: ALD-52, 1P-LSD, 1B-LSD, 1V-LSD, 1cP-LSD (in silico predictions only; no compound administered to animals)

handling.evidence: No in vivo experiments were conducted; in silico study only.

group_housing.evidence: No in vivo experiments were conducted; in silico study only.

day_night_flipped.evidence: No in vivo experiments were conducted; in silico study only.

enrichment_housing.evidence: No in vivo experiments were conducted; in silico study only.

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed that this paper contains no rodent behavioural assays — it is an entirely in silico/QSAR toxicological prediction study (ADMETlab 3.0, Percepta, STopTox, ProTox 3.0, VEGA, TEST 5.1.2, admetSAR 3.0, OCHEM).
Rat/mouse LD50 values in Table 3 are model-predicted, not experimentally measured; no compound was administered to any animal. Therefore `assays` is empty.
Head-twitch responses mentioned in the Introduction are citations of prior work (Halberstadt et al. 2020; Brandt et al. 2016, 2019, 2022), not experiments performed in this paper — not scored.
`dosing` left empty (candidate 'qwen' listed compounds with empty dose arrays, but the rubric restricts dosing entries to compounds actually administered to animals).
DOI taken from the Supplementary Information statement in the paper itself: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00204-025-04255-1.
species set to 'not_applicable' (candidates split between 'not_applicable', 'not_reported', and null); no live species was studied.
